name: The British invasion of Benin

summary.text: In January 1897 a British party under James Phillips, set on deposing the Oba, marched toward Benin City during a sacred festival and was ambushed at Ugbine; only two of its officers survived. Within weeks Rear-Admiral Harry Rawson led about 1,200 marines, sailors and protectorate troops in three columns on the city, which fell on 18 February. Three days later fire destroyed the palace and much of the city. Some 2,500 works of art, the Benin Bronzes among them, were carried off and sold. Oba Ovonramwen surrendered, was tried and exiled to Calabar, and died there in 1914, the year his son Eweka II was crowned.

routes.label: Phillips’ party sets out from Ughoton
The main column: up the Benin River to Warrigi, then overland via Ologbo
The Gwato column takes Gilli Gilli and Ughoton
The Sapoba column goes up the Jamieson river
About 2,500 bronzes, ivories and carvings shipped to Britain

moments.title: The ambush at Ugbine
moments.text: Phillips’ party, with some 250 men, presses on despite word that the Oba cannot receive visitors during the Ague festival. Benin warriors attack near Ugbine. Most of the officials and many porters are killed; Boisragon and Locke escape.

moments.title: The columns land
moments.text: The main column lands at Warrigi; the Gwato and Sapoba columns move up their creeks to divide Benin’s defenders.

moments.title: Benin City taken
moments.text: After days of fighting along the forest roads, the British use rockets in the final advance and the defenders withdraw.

moments.title: The city burns
moments.text: Fire destroys the palace and much of the city.

moments.title: The bronzes sold
moments.text: About 40 per cent of the looted works go to the British Museum; the rest are auctioned to pay for the expedition, many to museums in Germany.

moments.title: The Oba exiled
moments.text: Ovonramwen surrenders, is tried and deposed, and is exiled to Calabar with two of his wives. Six chiefs are hanged.

moments.title: Ologbosere hanged
moments.text: The war chief Ologbosere, who fought on from the forest, is captured and executed: the end of organised resistance.

moments.title: Eweka II crowned
moments.text: Months after Ovonramwen’s death in exile, his son is crowned Eweka II. He rebuilds the palace and the craft guilds.

note: Warrigi, Gilli Gilli, Sapoba and the creek mouths are placed approximately from period accounts.
